quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #14
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: If you stop at a railroad crossing with more than one track, what should you do?

options.text: Wait until you can see all tracks clearly before you move.
Stop on the first track and watch for another train.
Go through as soon as the train passes.
Go through when one track is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all tracks clearly before you move.
questions.explanation: Do not start moving as soon as a train passes. Wait until you can see all tracks clearly before you cross. Even with one track, check again for another train approaching.

questions.question: You notice your vehicle has a defect that may affect safety. What should you do?

options.text: Fix it as soon as possible.
Fix it when you have money.
Drive slower.
Drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fix it as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Fix any defect that affects safe operation right away. Do not drive the vehicle until it is fixed.

questions.question: When is a U-turn not permitted?

options.text: In a parking lot.
On or near a curve or hill.
On a straight road with clear view for 500 feet in both directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: On or near a curve or hill.
questions.explanation: Never turn around on or near a curve or hill. You cannot see oncoming traffic or pedestrians, which could cause a crash.

questions.question: Highway signs that tell you about dangerous conditions are called:

options.text: Regulatory signs.
Warning signs.
Information signs.
Guide signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning signs.
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert you to hazards ahead. Obey them for your safety. Ignoring a warning sign can cause an accident.

questions.question: A steady red arrow on a traffic light means:

options.text: You cannot turn in that direction.
You can turn in that direction after a complete stop.
You can turn in that direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot turn in that direction.
questions.explanation: A steady red arrow means you cannot move in that direction. Stop and wait for a green signal.

questions.question: Another driver is passing your car. What should you do?

options.text: Pull off the road.
Signal when it is safe for them to pass.
Check for oncoming traffic and slow down to help them pass safely.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for oncoming traffic and slow down to help them pass safely.
questions.explanation: Stay to the right when another driver passes on the left. Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed so they can move back into the right lane easily.

questions.question: How can you help prevent crashes?

options.text: Talk with other road users using signals and horn.
Ignore other drivers.
Drive only on back roads.
Avoid driving during rush hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Talk with other road users using signals and horn.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do unexpected things. Communicate with other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians by signaling when you slow down, stop, or turn. Use your horn or lights when needed.

questions.question: Your wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder. What should you do?

options.text: Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the road.
Stop your car on the edge of the road.
Slow down and carefully turn back onto the road.
Keep your speed and turn sharply back onto the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and carefully turn back onto the road.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed without hard braking and carefully steer back onto the pavement. Watch for traffic near you.

questions.question: ____ limit your focus, awareness, judgment, and memory.

options.text: Only a blood alcohol level above the legal limit can
Alcohol does not
Even a small amount of alcohol can
Only a blood alcohol level above 0.05 percent can

questions.correctAnswerText: Even a small amount of alcohol can
questions.explanation: Any amount of alcohol reduces your focus, awareness, judgment, and memory. Driving skills suffer right away. No one can drink and drive safely.

questions.question: Which of these must you obey first?

options.text: A red light
A police officer
A stop sign
A flashing red light

questions.correctAnswerText: A police officer
questions.explanation: A police officer's directions take priority over traffic signs, signals, and road markings. This also includes fire police, highway workers with flags, and school crossing guards.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: One-way traffic.
Two-way left turn.
Two-way traffic.
Minimum speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: One-way traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you the direction you must drive on a one-way street.

questions.question: Anything that requires you to ____ could cause you to crash.

options.text: Take your eyes off the road
Take your hands off the wheel
Take your attention away from driving
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: A distraction is anything that takes your attention, eyes, or hands away from driving.

questions.question: What does a red painted curb mean?

options.text: Loading zone.
The area is for picking up or dropping off passengers.
No parking, standing, or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: No parking, standing, or stopping.
questions.explanation: You cannot stop, stand, or park at a red painted curb.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down; curving road ahead.
Slow down and do not use your brakes.
Slow down; slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down; slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road becomes slippery when wet.

questions.question: If someone has drunk alcohol, what will help them overcome its effects?

options.text: Tomato juice and lime
Hot coffee
Fresh air
Only time

questions.correctAnswerText: Only time
questions.explanation: Only time will allow a person to recover from alcohol's effects.

questions.question: When you want to make a right turn, where should your car be?

options.text: Near the center of the street.
Close to the left side of the street.
Close to the right side of the street.
Past the center of the intersection when you begin to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close to the right side of the street.
questions.explanation: Before making a right turn, stay as far to the right as possible. Do not cut across lanes of traffic.

questions.question: When used on roadways, bicycles are considered:

options.text: Hazards.
Vehicles.
Dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicles.
questions.explanation: Bicycles are vehicles on roadways. Bicyclists and drivers must follow the same traffic rules.

questions.question: When driving in work zones, what should you do?

options.text: Increase your speed to get through as quickly as possible.
Reduce your speed and be ready to stop suddenly.
Keep your normal speed throughout the zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed and be ready to stop suddenly.
questions.explanation: In work zones, slow down and be ready to stop. Follow posted speed limits and watch for workers and changing conditions.

questions.question: A leaking exhaust system can:

options.text: Cause excessive oil use.
Require your vehicle to have a tune-up sooner.
Make you drowsy while driving.
Start grass fires on country roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make you drowsy while driving.
questions.explanation: Exhaust gases from a leaky system can cause drowsiness and are dangerous. They can be harmful or deadly in high amounts.

questions.question: You see a sign that says "Reduced speed, 35 mph." What does this mean?

options.text: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
The new 35 mph speed limit starts at the next speed limit sign.
You have plenty of time to slow down before the reduced speed zone.
You should reduce to 35 mph only in poor weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
questions.explanation: When a "Reduced speed" sign shows a new speed limit, that limit begins right at the sign.

questions.question: When a school bus has red lights flashing, vehicles behind it must stay stopped until:

options.text: All students are off the bus.
The stop arm is pulled back in.
The stop arm is pulled back in and the bus starts moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: The stop arm is pulled back in and the bus starts moving.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has red lights flashing and the stop arm is out, you must stay stopped. Only start driving when the lights turn off, the stop arm goes in, and the bus moves.

questions.question: When driving behind a large truck on the freeway, you should:

options.text: Drive closer than you would behind a regular car.
Drive farther back than you would behind a regular car.
Move to the right side of the truck and wait to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive farther back than you would behind a regular car.
questions.explanation: Large trucks have bigger blind spots. You need to leave more space behind a truck than behind a regular car.

questions.question: When a school bus is picking up or dropping off children, you must:

options.text: Stop, no matter which direction you are traveling.
Stop only if you are traveling in the same direction.
Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, no matter which direction you are traveling.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop before reaching a school bus that is picking up or dropping off children. This applies whether you are traveling in the same direction or the opposite direction.

questions.question: A driver entering the interstate from an entrance ramp should:

options.text: Let drivers already on the interstate go first.
Have the right-of-way.
Force their way into traffic.
Assume other drivers will move over for them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let drivers already on the interstate go first.
questions.explanation: When entering the interstate from a ramp, you must yield to drivers already on the highway. Wait for a safe gap and merge into traffic.

questions.question: Which of these is a safe driving technique?

options.text: Using high beam headlights in fog.
Staring at the road directly ahead.
Checking your rearview mirrors often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Checking your rearview mirrors often.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirrors every 2 to 5 seconds to stay alert. Do not just stare ahead. In fog, use low beam headlights, not high beams.

questions.question: Emergency vehicles:

options.text: Have the right-of-way when using sirens, horns, and flashing lights.
May use a loudspeaker to give instructions.
May follow each other.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must let police cars, fire trucks, and ambulances go first when they use sirens or horns and flashing red or blue lights. Follow their loudspeaker instructions. They often drive close together, so make sure the road is clear before moving.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when tires ride on water instead of the road. To prevent it in wet weather, you should:

options.text: Use cruise control to keep a steady speed.
Drive slower.
Move to the shoulder as soon as it rains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slower.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on wet roads. Slow down when the pavement is wet to prevent hydroplaning.

questions.question: What should you do if your gas pedal gets stuck while driving?

options.text: Reach down and try to pull it up.
Shift to park.
Shift to neutral and press the brake firmly.
Turn off the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to neutral and press the brake firmly.
questions.explanation: If your gas pedal sticks, keep your eyes on the road. Quickly shift to neutral and press the brake firmly. When safe, pull off the road and turn off the engine.

questions.question: When backing up, you should:

options.text: Look through the rear window.
Press hard on the gas pedal.
Only use your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: When backing up, put your right arm on the back of the passenger seat and look directly out the rear window. Do not rely only on mirrors because they do not show everything behind your car. Always back up slowly.

questions.question: When you see a school bus stopped with its stop arm out, you should:

options.text: Stop completely and wait before going forward.
Honk your horn before passing on the left.
Keep driving once you think most children are done exiting.
Pass the bus before its door opens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and wait before going forward.
questions.explanation: When you see a stopped school bus with its stop arm out, you must stop completely. Do not move until the stop arm is pulled in.

questions.question: A driver taking a non-prescription drug should:

options.text: Read the labels on the drug before driving.
Drink alcohol instead.
Continue to drive regardless of any warning labels.
Drive only during daylight hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: Read the labels on the drug before driving.
questions.explanation: Many over-the-counter medications can affect your ability to drive safely. Check the label for warnings about how the medication might affect you. If you are unsure, ask your doctor or pharmacist if you can drive safely while taking the medication.

questions.question: When is it illegal to drive below the speed limit?

options.text: When driving slowly disrupts the normal flow of traffic
When in heavy traffic in a construction zone
Only when driving in rural areas.
When driving under adverse weather conditions

questions.correctAnswerText: When driving slowly disrupts the normal flow of traffic
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive so slowly that you disrupt the normal flow of traffic. You may receive a ticket for driving too slowly.

questions.question: When it starts to sleet or snow, you should:

options.text: Keep your windshield and mirrors clear.
Allow extra distance between your vehicle and the vehicles you are following.
Approach all vehicles with caution.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: In snowy weather, keep your windshield and mirrors clear. Increase the space between your vehicle and others because a slippery road surface requires a longer distance to stop.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: One-way traffic.
Intersection ahead.
Merging traffic from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merging traffic from the right.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They alert you to conditions just ahead. This sign warns drivers to prepare for traffic merging safely from the right.

questions.question: Is it legal to cross a double solid yellow centerline to pass?

options.text: Yes.
No.
If there is no oncoming traffic.
If the vehicle ahead is driving under the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: No.
questions.explanation: Two solid yellow lines mean traffic in both directions cannot cross them unless turning into a driveway or business entrance. No passing is allowed over a solid yellow line.

questions.question: You must stop for a school bus:

options.text: That is parked on the shoulder with no one in it.
When it approaches you, even if its lights are not flashing.
If you are both driving on a two-lane highway and its red lights are flashing.
Whenever the driver waves at you.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you are both driving on a two-lane highway and its red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: You must stop when a school bus displays flashing red lights while picking up or dropping off children. On a two-lane road, traffic in both directions must stop while the red lights are flashing and the stop arm is extended.

questions.question: Your tire blows out while driving. You should:

options.text: Slam on your brakes.
Hold your steering wheel tightly and slow to a stop.
Keep driving normally.
Turn on your emergency flashers and continue driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold your steering wheel tightly and slow to a stop.
questions.explanation: Do not immediately apply the brakes. Grip the steering wheel firmly and stay in your lane. Slow down gradually by releasing the accelerator. Once you are moving slowly, apply the brakes lightly and pull off the road safely.

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle is using its siren and flashing lights, you must yield by:

options.text: Driving to the right edge of the road and stopping.
Moving to the right lane and driving slowly until it passes.
Stopping immediately, even if you are in an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving to the right edge of the road and stopping.
questions.explanation: You must yield to any emergency vehicle using its siren and flashing lights. Drive to the right edge of the road and stop, but avoid stopping in an intersection. You can move again after the emergency vehicle passes.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you can check your blind spot by:

options.text: Using the inside rearview mirror.
Turning your head and looking over your shoulder.
Using your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turning your head and looking over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Even with mirrors, there are blind spots you cannot see. Before changing lanes, look over your shoulder to check these areas.

questions.question: If a child is riding a bicycle near your vehicle:

options.text: Beep your horn.
Expect the child to be in total control of the bicycle.
Expect the unexpected.

questions.correctAnswerText: Expect the unexpected.
questions.explanation: Children on bicycles are unpredictable and often make sudden changes in direction. Young riders are especially likely to swerve without warning. Children and bicycles are small and can be hard to see.

questions.question: What does Wisconsin's Implied Consent Law mean?

options.text: Drivers under 21 cannot drive after drinking any alcohol.
Penalties are stricter after a first OWI conviction.
You must take an alcohol test if a police officer asks you to.
A second OWI conviction requires an ignition interlock device in your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must take an alcohol test if a police officer asks you to.
questions.explanation: The Implied Consent Law means that by driving in Wisconsin, you agree to take an alcohol test when asked. If you refuse, you will be arrested. You will lose your driving privileges for at least one year, plus face other penalties.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop for other traffic.
Traffic is merging in. Give them space to merge safely.
Traffic is merging in. Keep to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic is merging in. Give them space to merge safely.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that traffic is entering from another road. Check your side and rear mirrors. Move to another lane if you can to give merging drivers a clear path.

questions.question: If oncoming headlights are blinding you at night, what should you do?

options.text: Look toward the right edge of the road.
Switch to high beams.
Turn your lights on and off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: Look at the right edge of the road instead of looking straight ahead. This keeps your car on the road safely until you pass the oncoming vehicle.

questions.question: You are driving on a one-way street. When can you turn left onto another one-way street?

options.text: When you increase your speed before turning.
When traffic on that street moves to the right.
When traffic on that street moves to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: When traffic on that street moves to the left.
questions.explanation: You can turn left onto a one-way street if traffic moves to the left and no sign forbids it. You cannot turn left onto a one-way street where traffic moves to the right.

questions.question: If you see orange construction signs and cones on a freeway, you must:

options.text: Slow down because a lane ends ahead.
Be ready for workers and equipment ahead.
Change lanes and keep your current speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for workers and equipment ahead.
questions.explanation: In work zones, signs warn you about workers, slow equipment, and closed lanes. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What do speed limit signs tell you?

options.text: Possible speeds for the area.
The fastest or slowest speed you are allowed to drive.
The speed to drive in heavy traffic.
The speed to drive in poor conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The fastest or slowest speed you are allowed to drive.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs show the maximum or minimum safe speed allowed on a road. The maximum is for ideal conditions. You must drive slower when conditions require it.

questions.question: If you drink alcohol socially, how can you drive safely?

options.text: Drink coffee before driving.
Get a ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.
Take a cold shower before driving.
Stop drinking 30 minutes before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get a ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.
questions.explanation: The best way to avoid driving impaired is to get a ride with someone who has not drunk alcohol. Coffee and cold showers do not lower your blood alcohol level. Your body takes about one hour to process one drink.

questions.question: When you see this yellow sign, what should you do?

options.text: Always stop at the crosswalk.
Stop at the crosswalk until a crossing guard signals you to go.
Be ready to stop if children are in the crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if children are in the crosswalk.
questions.explanation: This five-sided sign means you are near a school. Watch for children and stop if any are in the crosswalk.

questions.question: When should you not use your horn?

options.text: When you cannot see far ahead.
If you might hit another vehicle.
Near blind pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near blind pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Do not use your horn near blind pedestrians. It can be dangerous. Let them cross safely.

questions.question: Why should you watch carefully for motorcycles?

options.text: They are harder to see than cars.
They rarely use their headlights.
Motorcyclists are less skilled drivers.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are harder to see than cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are smaller and harder to see. They can hide in your blind spot. It is hard to judge distance and speed with a motorcycle. Always be alert around them.
